name: Red Burlap Bandana
summary: In Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem gathers red bandanas from slain Defias thieves near the abbey vineyards. The cloth marks low-ranking highwaymen and cutpurses of the Brotherhood.

sections.title: A Mark of the Brotherhood
sections.body: Red burlap masks mark the Defias Brotherhood's rank-and-file. Cheap, rough cloth dyed red hides a thief's features and signals allegiance to the growing rebellion. In Northshire, young recruits and common thugs carry these scarves into the eastern orchards. The local guards recognize the striking red fabric as proof of thieves slain nearby.

faq.q: Why does Deputy Willem want these bandanas?
faq.answer: Deputy Willem collects the bandanas as proof that an adventurer has killed Defias thugs near Northshire Abbey. The thieves wear the red cloth openly, confirming the bounty has been claimed.

faq.q: Who wears the red burlap bandanas?
faq.answer: Footpads and thugs of the Defias Brotherhood wear the red burlap bandanas. The coarse cloth conceals their faces and marks their loyalty to the outlaws.

faq.q: Why are Defias thieves operating in Northshire?
faq.answer: Defias scouts and brigands camp across the stream east of Northshire Abbey to scavenge and steal supplies. The abbey garrison is stretched thin, leaving the nearby orchards open to highwaymen.
Cheap burlap treated with crimson dye gives the bandanas their red color. The hue is the Defias Brotherhood's banner and uniform, so members can recognize one another in the field.

angles.text: As a developing rogue, you can learn from Northshire's clumsy footpads how quickly undisciplined outlaws become easy targets for local law enforcement.
As an Alliance member, you can see the red bandanas reaching Northshire Abbey's doorstep as a sign that Stormwind is losing control of the kingdom's rural borders.
